children.game_version: A safe tag-style game mimicking the separation and meeting of dancers without weapons

seniors.counts: Basic slow-to-fast counts based on source acceleration
seniors.seated_version: Seated foot-tapping maintaining the accelerating tempo concept
seniors.standing_version: Supported standing balance drill without jumps or axes
seniors.tempo_and_range: Reduced tempo and eliminated low squatting and jumping ranges

feedback_rules.description: Distinguish between the slow initial footwork phase and the rapid acceleration phase

learning_units.description: Execute the opening subtle ground-level foot movements

prerequisites.description: Basic lower body agility for squatting and jumping motions

social_formats.description: Solo performance or group formation with paired mock duels using a valaška or long stick

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: danced with the Valaška in most regions, or a long stick in some Eastern Slovak regions
movement_profile.footwork: begins with subtle foot movements that become more dramatic and fast paced
movement_profile.formation_and_space: solo or with a group of dancers together, where two dancers will separate and come together to perform a mock duel
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: features some elements of dancing that is slightly similar to more eastern squat dances
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: jumping and ducking movements, squat dances
movement_profile.partnering: mock duel featuring jumping and ducking movements where one dancer aims for the head and the other aims for the lower legs

signature_moves.description: Two dancers separate and come together to perform a mock duel featuring jumping and ducking with one aiming for the head and the other for the lower legs.
signature_moves.name: Valaška mock duel

movement_profile.tempo_feel: starts out slow and gets faster as the dance goes on

music_profile.rhythm_pattern: starts out slow and gets faster as the dance goes on
music_profile.sound_description: Played in a traditional Moravian or Slovak style formation featuring string instruments and the cimbalom, accompanied frequently by the distinctive breathy tones of the fujara and koncovka.

basic_steps: Subtle foot movements close to the ground
teaching.formation: Solo or group of dancers together, with two dancers separating for a mock duel
teaching.level_notes: Begins slow and gets faster as the dance goes on
